pitch: Greenland looks as big as India on the map. It isn't.
hints: Belief: on the classroom/Google map Greenland looks as big as (or bigger than) India. Owners: Greenland's area from the Government of Greenland / Statistics Greenland or the UN Statistics Division Demographic Yearbook; India's 3,287,263 km² from Survey of India / Census. Mercator scale factor at each latitude is OUR computation (method/). Felt comparison: how many Greenlands fit in India, or Greenland vs an Indian region. Human detail from a primary source.

pitch: At Varanasi the Ganga flows north, back towards the mountains
hints: ⚑ religion (Uttaravahini belief). Belief: the Ganga flows from the Himalaya south-east to the sea. Test the geometry ourselves from official river geometry (Natural Earth / India-WRIS / Survey of India) at Varanasi: bearing and length of the northward stretch (method/). Owners for any religious significance: UP government / Varanasi official pages, credited as belief. No borders drawn.

pitch: The 'Arabic' numerals on your phone are Indian
hints: ⚑ cultural-origin claims. Test it. Owners: primary texts and holders: Al-Khwarizmi's treatise (Latin 'Algoritmi de numero Indorum'), Fibonacci's Liber Abaci 1202 ('modus Indorum'), Bodleian Library's 2017 Bakhshali manuscript radiocarbon dates. Say exactly what each proves (digits vs zero vs place value). No nationalist overstatement.

pitch: In Meghalaya people grow bridges instead of building them
hints: Owners: India's UNESCO Tentative List entry 'Jingkieng Jri: Living Root Bridge Cultural Landscapes' (2022), Meghalaya government, peer-reviewed papers (e.g. Ludwig et al. 2023 on root bridges, Scientific Reports/others). Numbers: how many bridges/villages, tree species, how long they take to grow. Map: East Khasi/West Jaintia hills, Meghalaya; rainfall link (Cherrapunji/Mawsynram from IMD) only if verified.

pitch: How a British plant hunter took tea from China to India
hints: ⚑ colonial history. Owners: Robert Fortune's own book 'A Journey to the Tea Countries of China' (1852) for what he took and when; East India Company records; Tea Board of India for today's production. Test the twist: much of India's tea comes from the native Assam variety (discovered 1823-34), not Fortune's China plants. Say who says what.

pitch: Indian trains once ran on three different track widths
hints: Owners: Indian Railways Year Book / Ministry of Railways (route km by gauge, then and now; Project Unigauge from 1992), Railway Board. Gauges: 1,676 mm broad, 1,000 mm metre, 762/610 mm narrow. Hidden number: what share is broad gauge now; what heritage narrow lines remain.

pitch: Puducherry is one place, right? It's four pieces in three states
hints: ⚑ borders (internal). Owners: Census of India 2011 district areas (Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam), Government of Puducherry, the 1962 treaty of cession (MEA) / 1954 de facto transfer. Distances between the four pieces: OUR measurement (great-circle). Show no border lines (house rule: maps draw no borders); use pins and outlines of the pieces only.

Owners: Gazetteer of Bombay City and Island (1909), Maharashtra State Gazetteers, MCGM. Test the 'seven islands' list and the reclamation steps (Hornby Vellard 1782-84 etc.). Map: Sentinel-2 / relief of today's Mumbai with the old island outlines ONLY if from a primary historical map with a clear source, else label 'illustrative'.

pitch: How one boulder shielded Kedarnath temple in 2013
hints: ⚑ religion; disaster deaths. Owners: Geological Survey of India report on the June 2013 Kedarnath disaster, Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology papers (e.g. Dobhal et al. 2013, Current Science), NDMA. Test whether the boulder deflected debris (who says so). Use official death toll wording with its author; no sensational framing.

pitch: India has a long coast but few natural harbours
hints: Test it: define 'natural harbour' from an authority (e.g. NHO / Ministry of Ports or a port's own history). Owners: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (major ports list), each port trust's own history page (e.g. Chennai's artificial harbour, Visakhapatnam's natural one, Mumbai). Coastline length from the 2023-24 re-assessment (Rajya Sabha) if used. Avoid any claim the sources don't make.

pitch: Why Roman coins keep turning up in Tamil Nadu
hints: Owners: Pliny the Elder, Natural History 12.84 (the 'drain to India' complaint) in a standard translation; the Muziris papyrus (Vienna); Government Museum Chennai / ASI hoard reports (e.g. Pudukottai, Arikamedu excavation reports). Counts of hoards/coins only from a primary catalogue. Map: hoard sites as pins.

pitch: One Indian park holds most of the world's one-horned rhinos
hints: Owners: Assam Forest Department rhino estimation (2022: count), IUCN SSC Asian Rhino Specialist Group / CITES CoP report for the world total, Kaziranga National Park authority. Compute the share with one year and basis. Recovery story numbers (early 1900s) only from a primary source.

pitch: How many Indias fit inside Russia?
hints: Owners: UNSD Demographic Yearbook areas (Russia, India) or national statistics; OUR computation of the ratio and of the Mercator exaggeration (method/). Different from W4-01: this one gives the true count, and the felt comparison. Show no borders; true-scale outline moves only.

pitch: Guess the Indian river from its route
hints: Quiz (engine G3). Choose THREE famous rivers other than the Ganga (used in W4-02) whose courses are distinctive (e.g. Narmada flows west, Brahmaputra's U-turn, Godavari/Kaveri). River geometry from Natural Earth / India-WRIS; one verified surprising fact per river (lengths from CWC / India-WRIS). No borders.
